title: Radial Basis Function and Kernel Trick

cards.question: What advantage does the Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernel provide in Support Vector Machines?
cards.answer: The RBF kernel allows for non-linear decision boundaries by mapping input space into a higher-dimensional space where linear separation is feasible.

cards.text: The RBF kernel is known for its ability to handle {{non-linear decision boundaries}}.
cards.hint: characteristic of RBF kernel in separating data

cards.question: Why is the RBF kernel considered computationally intensive?

options.B: It demands extra memory for data storage.
options.C: It involves operations in higher-dimensional space.
options.D: It needs more complex algorithms to process data.

cards.explanation: The RBF kernel involves high-dimensional space computations, making it computationally intensive.

cards.question: What role does the Kernel Trick play in using the RBF kernel with Support Vector Machines?
cards.answer: The Kernel Trick allows computations of the RBF kernel to be performed implicitly, making them more computationally feasible.

cards.text: The {{Kernel Trick}} allows implicit computation of high-dimensional space operations in the RBF kernel.
cards.hint: technique used to improve RBF kernel efficiency
